questions.q: The main purpose of a political party's manifesto is to
options: present the party's policies and programmes to the electorate
record the names of members who have paid their dues
serve as the party's internal constitution and rules
publish the results of the party's primary elections
questions.explanation: A manifesto sets out what a party promises to do if it wins office, so it is mainly a statement of policies and programmes. A membership register, party constitution and primary results are internal records rather than a public programme of government.

questions.q: A constitution made by a colonial authority or military government and not ratified by the people is best described as
questions.explanation: An imposed constitution is handed down by an external or undemocratic authority without popular approval. An autochthonous constitution is the opposite kind, because it is home-grown and derives from the people, while federal and flexible describe structure and amendment procedure rather than origin.

questions.q: The administrative head of the United Nations, who directs the Secretariat and serves as the organisation's chief spokesperson, is the
options: Registrar of the International Court of Justice
questions.explanation: The Secretary-General heads the United Nations Secretariat and performs the organisation's main administrative and diplomatic functions. The President of the General Assembly and the President of the Security Council preside over particular organs, while the Registrar manages the court's registry.

questions.q: A government controls the armed forces and civil service, and most citizens accept that it has the right to rule even when they disagree with its policies. This acceptance is an example of
questions.explanation: Legitimacy is the belief by citizens that a government has the right to rule, which encourages voluntary obedience. Sovereignty is supreme legal authority, while power is the capacity to compel compliance; a government may have power without being accepted as rightful.

questions.q: The 1954 Constitution is regarded as a landmark in Nigeria’s constitutional development because it
options: introduced the elective principle for the first time
created the office of a ceremonial president
entrenched a bill of rights enforceable in the courts
established a federal system with regional governments as constituent units
questions.explanation: The 1954 Constitution formally established a federal arrangement in which the central government and the regions exercised defined powers. The elective principle had been introduced earlier by the Clifford Constitution, while a ceremonial president came with the 1963 Republican Constitution.

questions.q: A High Court in Ibadan decides a case by following an earlier decision of the Supreme Court on the same point of law. This practice illustrates the principle of
questions.explanation: The High Court follows the Supreme Court's earlier decision because lower courts are bound by the decisions of higher courts under the doctrine of judicial precedent. Judicial review concerns the power of courts to examine the constitutionality of acts, not the mere following of a previous decision.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution, legislative powers in relation to the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, are exercised by the
questions.explanation: By the 1999 Constitution, the Federal Capital Territory is treated like a state for many purposes, but legislative powers in relation to it are vested in the National Assembly. The Federal Capital Territory Administration implements policies; it does not replace the National Assembly as the law-making body for the territory.

questions.q: The presentation of the annual budget by the President to the National Assembly is an important constitutional practice because it enables the legislature to
options: examine and approve proposed government revenue and expenditure
take over the day-to-day running of ministries
enable the President to make laws without the National Assembly
prevent the judiciary from interpreting the Appropriation Act
questions.explanation: The annual budget presentation allows the legislature to exercise its control over public funds by examining and approving proposed revenue and expenditure. It does not transfer law-making power to the President or give the legislature the duty of running ministries day to day.

questions.q: The Academic Staff Union of Universities presents a memorandum to the Federal Government demanding better funding of public universities. This activity by the union is best described as
questions.explanation: The union is expressing and pressing the demands of its members before government, which is interest articulation by a pressure group. Political recruitment would involve selecting persons for public office, while constitutional amendment and judicial review are not the activity described.

questions.q: A law made by a State House of Assembly authorises the police to detain a suspect for 72 hours without taking the person to court. If this law conflicts with the Constitution, it is
options: valid because the State House of Assembly has power to make laws on police detention
valid until a magistrate court declares it unconstitutional
void to the extent of its inconsistency with the Constitution
enforceable because police powers are on the residual list
questions.explanation: The Constitution is supreme, and any law that conflicts with it is void to the extent of the inconsistency. A court declaration may confirm this position, but the inconsistency itself is what makes the law invalid.

questions.q: The Code of Conduct Bureau is established under the 1999 Constitution mainly to
options: nominate persons for appointment as judges
interpret the Constitution in disputes between governments
receive and examine declarations of assets and liabilities made by public officers
conduct free and fair elections into public offices
questions.explanation: The Code of Conduct Bureau is a constitutional body charged mainly with receiving and examining declarations of assets and liabilities made by public officers. It does not conduct elections, interpret the Constitution or appoint judges.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: When the National Assembly re-passes a bill with a two-thirds majority in each House after the President has refused to give assent, the legislature is exercising
questions.explanation: Re-passing a bill by the required two-thirds majority in each House after the President refuses assent is an override of the presidential veto. This is a legislative check on the executive rather than delegated legislation or judicial review.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The Supreme Court nullifies a directive issued by a minister as inconsistent with the Constitution. This action best illustrates
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court is reviewing an executive directive against the standard set by the Constitution and nullifying it for inconsistency. This is judicial review of executive action, not parliamentary control or delegation of legislative power.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The requirement that the President's appointment of ambassadors be confirmed by the Senate is best explained as
options: a rule that makes the President answerable to the Senate for daily administration
a means by which the judiciary supervises foreign policy
a legislative check on executive appointments
questions.explanation: Senate confirmation of ambassadorial appointments gives the legislature a share in checking executive appointments under the principle of checks and balances. It does not amount to delegated legislation, judicial supervision of foreign policy or Senate management of daily administration.

questions.q: The organ of the United Nations that elects the non-permanent members of the Security Council is the
questions.explanation: Non-permanent members of the Security Council are elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms. The Economic and Social Council coordinates economic and social matters and does not elect Security Council members.

questions.q: The Chairperson of the African Union Commission is elected by the
options: Assembly of Heads of State and Government
questions.explanation: The Assembly of Heads of State and Government is the AU’s highest decision-making organ and elects the Chairperson of the Commission. The Pan-African Parliament, Executive Council and Peace and Security Council have other representative, advisory or security functions.

questions.q: A historian notes that in the 1920s a small number of residents of Lagos could elect representatives to the Legislative Council for the first time. This innovation was introduced by the
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 introduced limited elective representation to the Legislative Council, with elections in Lagos and Calabar. The Richards, Macpherson and Lyttleton constitutions came later and developed representative institutions but did not initiate the elective principle.

questions.q: When Musa, a wealthy businessman in Akure who holds no public office, uses his money to influence the selection of a party’s candidate, his influence is best described as
questions.explanation: Musa can affect decisions because of his resources, but he has no recognised public office or legal right to command, so he exercises power without authority. Legitimate, traditional and legal-rational authority all require a socially or legally accepted right to rule.

questions.q: A Nigerian student in London is arrested and the Nigerian High Commission sends an official to ensure that she is treated according to law. This action is an example of
questions.explanation: Consular protection involves a home state’s officials helping its citizens abroad and ensuring lawful treatment in criminal or administrative matters. Economic diplomacy concerns trade and investment, while shuttle diplomacy involves a mediator moving between parties in a dispute.

questions.q: The military government that announced the creation of seven new states, bringing the number of states in Nigeria to nineteen, was headed by
questions.explanation: The announcement was made on 3 February 1976 under General Murtala Muhammed, increasing the number of states in Nigeria to nineteen. Obasanjo succeeded Murtala after the 13 February 1976 coup and did not make that announcement.

questions.q: Which body served as the highest ruling organ of the Nigerian military government under General Ibrahim Babangida?
questions.explanation: Babangida's administration used the Armed Forces Ruling Council as the top decision-making body after 1985. The Supreme Military Council belonged to earlier military regimes, while the Provisional Ruling Council was associated with the Sani Abacha era.

questions.q: A body that seeks to influence government policies in favour of its members but does not seek to contest elections in order to form a government is called a
questions.explanation: A pressure group, such as a trade union or professional association, tries to shape public policy through lobbying, campaigns and public opinion without nominating candidates to form a government. A political party, by contrast, seeks to win elections and control government.

questions.q: Election observers in Kaduna note that party agents were barred from observing the counting of votes. This is most likely to undermine
options: the principle of universal adult suffrage
transparency and confidence in the electoral process
questions.explanation: Party agents and observers help to assure the public that counting is done openly and accurately. Barring them from observing counting weakens transparency, even if voters cast their ballots secretly.

questions.q: Which of the following is the clearest feature of a one-party system?
options: Elections are conducted only by the judiciary
Several parties exist, but one enjoys public funding
Only one political party is legally permitted to operate and compete for power
The ruling party shares cabinet posts with rival parties
questions.explanation: In a one-party system, the law allows only one political party to exist and seek power. The existence of several parties, even with one dominant party, is different from a legal one-party system.

questions.q: The Association of Nigerian Market Women in Oyo State stages a peaceful march to the state House of Assembly to oppose a new levy. This activity is best described as
options: direct action by a pressure group
questions.explanation: A peaceful march is a form of direct action used by a pressure group to draw attention to its demands and influence government policy. The group is not seeking to contest elections, so the action is not political recruitment or a primary election.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: In Nigeria, the National Judicial Council recommends candidates for judicial appointment, while the Senate confirms the Chief Justice of Nigeria. This arrangement is best understood as a means of...
options: sharing appointment powers to check arbitrariness and protect judicial independence
allowing the legislature to decide cases that come before the courts
making the judiciary subordinate to the Senate in the performance of its duties
concentrating judicial appointments in the executive for efficiency
questions.explanation: The National Judicial Council screens judicial candidates while the Senate confirms the Chief Justice, so no single branch completely controls judicial appointments. This mutual involvement is a check that helps guard judicial independence rather than subject courts to either the executive or the legislature.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The National Assembly invites the Minister of Finance to explain how ₦15 billion allocated to a road project was spent. This action is an exercise of...
options: executive control over the legislature's power of appropriation
delegation of legislative authority to the executive
questions.explanation: Summoning a minister to account for public funds is part of the National Assembly's oversight and checks on the executive. It is not judicial review, nor does it transfer legislative power to the minister.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: A High Court in Enugu nullifies a levy introduced by the Enugu State House of Assembly because the law did not follow the procedure prescribed by the Constitution. This is an illustration of...
options: delegation of legislative powers to the courts
judicial review as a check on legislative action
questions.explanation: The court is examining whether a law complied with the Constitution and invalidating it when it did not, which is judicial review. This checks the legislature and upholds constitutional supremacy.

questions.q: The Economic, Social and Cultural Council of the African Union was established mainly to...
options: try individuals accused of war crimes on the continent
give civil society organisations a formal voice in the African Union's affairs
command the African Standby Force during armed conflicts
elect the Chairperson of the African Union Commission
questions.explanation: ECOSOCC is an advisory organ designed to involve civil society groups in the work of the African Union. It does not command troops, elect the Commission Chairperson, or try war crimes suspects.

questions.q: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, has its seat in...
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice sits at the Peace Palace in The Hague. New York hosts the UN Headquarters, but not the World Court.

questions.q: Nigeria appoints Mr Adebayo as its principal diplomatic representative to Ghana. His official title is...
questions.explanation: Nigeria and Ghana are both Commonwealth members, so their principal diplomatic representatives are called High Commissioners rather than Ambassadors. A Consul-General handles consular matters, not the overall diplomatic mission.

questions.q: One of Nigeria's foreign policy objectives stated in the 1999 Constitution is to...
options: promote African integration and support African unity
secure permanent membership of the United Nations Security Council
give precedence to European affairs over African matters
maintain military alliances only with Western powers
questions.explanation: Section 19 of the 1999 Constitution includes the promotion of African integration and support for African unity among Nigeria's foreign policy objectives. Permanent UN Security Council membership is not stated there, and Nigeria's policy is not to subordinate African affairs to Europe.

questions.q: A state government relocates a market in Keffi. Traders comply only after the High Court confirms that the relocation notice follows the enabling law. The traders' obedience is based mainly on
questions.explanation: Compliance rests on established laws and court confirmation, which fits legal-rational authority. Charismatic authority rests on personal appeal, while traditional authority rests on custom.

questions.q: During military rule in Nigeria, decrees often contained ouster clauses. These clauses were significant because they
options: required judges to approve all decrees before publication
transferred judicial powers to traditional rulers
restricted the courts from inquiring into the validity of government actions
made decrees subject to review by the National Assembly
questions.explanation: Ouster clauses sought to exclude judicial review of certain decrees and government actions. They did not make decrees subject to the National Assembly, which was not functioning as a normal legislature under military rule.

questions.q: A major reason some Nigerian military regimes kept postponing programmes for returning to civilian rule was that
options: civilian politicians had refused to register political parties
continued military control enabled them to retain power and influence
the armed forces were constitutionally barred from governing
foreign governments insisted on military administration
questions.explanation: Prolonged transition programmes allowed military rulers to remain in office and shape political arrangements. The other claims reverse the usual situation, since military regimes often controlled the transition process rather than being forced to stay by foreign insistence.

questions.q: A country using a party-list proportional representation system sets an electoral threshold of 5 per cent. A party that receives 4 per cent of the valid national votes will
options: be restricted to contesting only local elections
receive no seats under the proportional allocation
receive five per cent of the seats in the legislature
be given an automatic run-off against the largest party
questions.explanation: An electoral threshold excludes parties whose share of the vote falls below the stated minimum from participating in the allocation of seats. A party with 4 per cent therefore fails the 5 per cent threshold; the threshold is not a rule granting a fixed share of seats or a run-off.

questions.q: At a polling unit in Minna, the electoral officer who supervises accreditation, voting and counting is known as the
questions.explanation: The presiding officer is in charge of a polling unit and oversees the voting and counting up to the declaration of results for that unit. A returning officer handles the collation and return of results for a wider constituency, while a party agent represents a candidate.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, judicial powers are vested in the courts. This means that the courts have the authority to
options: remove the President through a simple majority vote
control the day-to-day administration of ministries
make laws for the federation through court orders
interpret the law and decide disputes according to law
questions.explanation: Judicial power is the authority of courts to interpret laws, hear disputes and administer justice according to law. Making general laws is the work of the legislature, while controlling ministries belongs to the executive, and the President is not removed by a simple court or majority vote.

questions.q: A youth group in the Niger Delta vandalises oil pipelines and threatens further attacks unless the government provides roads and employment for its community. In political science, the group is best described as
questions.explanation: Anomic pressure groups pursue their demands through violent or unlawful action, often outside normal channels. Institutional groups operate within bodies such as the armed forces, while promotional groups campaign for public causes by peaceful means.

questions.q: The main peaceful means through which the Bakassi Peninsula dispute between Nigeria and Cameroon was settled was...
options: economic sanctions imposed by the African Union
adjudication by the International Court of Justice
questions.explanation: The dispute was submitted for adjudication and the International Court of Justice delivered a ruling which Nigeria accepted, followed by withdrawal arrangements. Permanent military occupation and economic sanctions are coercive measures, while Commonwealth mediation was not the principal settlement route.
